title: data: normalise boolean fields already stored as the text 'true'/'false' (SQL driver), so equality filters find rows written before #34965
body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Filed by triage at the request of repo:objectstack#3: a follow-up of p1 #34916 (PR #34965), ruled out of that PR's scope (seat ruling 6957305509; L1-d 6959775843).

## What happens

Before #34965, inline grid edit on the SQL driver stored boolean fields as the text `'true'` / `'false'`. #34965 fixes the write, and the read of a stored `'false'` / `'0'`.

Rows already written that way still hold text. An equality filter such as `won = false` (and `requiredWhen` over such rows in queries) keeps missing them until each row is re-saved.

## Done when

- A one-off normalisation (migration or upgrade step) rewrites text-stored booleans to the driver's boolean form, idempotently and per object.
- Or, if the dev finds a read-side fix that makes filters match both forms cheaply, that instead, with the reason recorded.
- A pin: a row seeded with `'false'` text is found by `= false` after the step.

Grade: **p1 · domain:server**. The theme is install, upgrade and uninstall reliability (an upgrade step), plus epic #34571's console data. The named effect is the same one #34916 was graded p1 for, filters silently miss rows, and it stays live for existing data until this lands.

Blocked-by: #34916 (land PR #34965 first, so new writes stop adding text rows)
